Somos dos estudiantes, una de Ingeniería Industrial y otra de Sociología, unidas por el interés en la innovación, la investigación, la tecnología y la búsqueda de soluciones a problemas reales.

Estamos formando MENTES BRILLANTES para participar en el NASA Space Apps Challenge. Buscamos personas creativas, comprometidas, curiosas y con iniciativa, especialmente con habilidades en programación, diseño, ciencias, análisis de datos y desarrollo tecnológico.
summary:
GeoTen is a static web application that detects and measures trends in Earth science variables, such as temperature, precipitation, air humidity, wind, solar radiation, and soil moisture. It allows users to determine which variable is changing, where, at what rate, and whether that change is statistically significant.
The application works with data from the NASA POWER API or with CSV files provided by the user. It applies the Mann-Kendall test, the Sen slope, and false discovery rate (FDR) correction to this data, and presents the results on an interactive map and in graphs, along with an explanation in plain language. It opens in any modern browser and requires no installation or server.
details:
GeoTen is a free web application that allows users to detect, measure, and visualize trends in Earth science variables, such as temperature, precipitation, air humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, and soil moisture. It works by collecting data from the NASA POWER API or by uploading your own files in CSV format. It then applies statistical methods such as the Mann-Kendall test, Sen’s slope, and FDR correction to determine whether a variable is increasing, decreasing, or remaining stable, as well as the magnitude and significance of these changes. The results are presented through interactive maps, graphs, and simple explanations.

GeoTen makes it easy to analyze climate data without the need to purchase specialized software or have advanced statistical knowledge. It enables students, researchers, environmental technicians, farmers, and water resource managers to obtain reliable information to understand environmental changes and support decision-making.

The project aims to contribute to climate change monitoring and the sustainable management of natural resources. Its impact is primarily related to SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). It also aims to make NASA’s scientific data accessible to communities and individuals who can use it to understand their environment and anticipate potential environmental risks.

To develop GeoTen, Visual Studio Code was used as the code editor, with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript as the primary programming languages. The NASA POWER API was integrated to obtain environmental information, Leaflet was used to create interactive maps, and Chart.js was used to generate charts. Python was also used with the pymannkendall library to verify the statistical results. The application was published via Netlify and was supported by Claude Code, an AI-powered coding assistant. No proprietary hardware or sensors were used.

GeoTen stands out for integrating scientific statistical methods into a simple, free web application accessible from any browser. Its main innovation lies in combining trend analysis, geographic visualization, and automatic interpretation of results into a single tool, without relying on servers or installations. Additionally, it incorporates mechanisms to reduce false statistical conclusions and presents the information in understandable language.

The following factors were taken into account: data reliability, the accuracy of statistical methods, ease of use, accessibility, environmental impact, and user needs. Compatibility with different data sources, validation of results through statistical tests, and the possibility of expanding the tool with new environmental variables and data sources in the future were also considered.
